title: Two pointers: sorted pair sum
summary: Indices of two values in a sorted list that sum to target, or None. Too small: values[left] can't pair with anything left, so drop it; too big: drop values[right]. O(n), O(1) space.
code: # Move inward using the sorted order.
triggers: sorted input and a pair or triple with a target sum or difference
discard candidates from both ends in O(1) extra space
prompts: Gift cards come in sorted denominations. Find two different cards that together cover a bill exactly.
Package weights are listed in increasing order. Pick two different packages whose weights exactly fill the space left on a truck.
invariant: Every pair that can still reach target lies inside values[left..right]; everything outside has been ruled out.
mantra: Sum too small: move left up. Too big: move right down.
pitfalls: Only valid on sorted input; sorting first loses the original indices.
while left < right, not <=: an element can't pair with itself.
3Sum: sort, fix one value, run this on the rest, and skip equal neighbours.

anchors.name: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
anchors.trick: Exactly this; the answer uses 1-based indices.

anchors.name: 3Sum
anchors.trick: Fix i, two-pointer the rest, skip duplicates of i and of left.

anchors.name: Container With Most Water
anchors.trick: Move the shorter side inward: the taller one can't help a narrower container.

mutations.explanation: Lets left meet right, so one element pairs with itself when twice its value equals target.
Moves the wrong pointer: a sum that is too small drops the largest value and misses real pairs.
